Thanks, Sofia.

Short answer: yes, we should get a completed W-8BEN-E from Portsmith if they are a foreign corporate payee providing services to Redwood. That will document their foreign status and generally exempt the payment from U.S. 1099 reporting.

Checklist from finance/legal: 
- Fully completed and signed W-8BEN-E (preferably with page numbers and handwritten signature).
- Corporate name on the W-8BEN-E must match the invoice and the beneficiary name on the bank details.
- A copy of the company registration or VAT cert is useful for identity proof (they already provided VAT cert).
- Bank details and a bank statement or payment instruction with the company name (we use that to validate beneficiary match).

Laura — can Payments hold payment until we receive the signed W-8BEN-E + bank proof? We can send a standardized request to the vendor (template below) to speed this up. If we do not receive W-8, we may need to treat them as reportable and issue 1099 — or in some cases apply backup withholding, but that's last resort.

Marcus — FYI in case any treaty/withholding nuance is needed for freight services (I believe freight is generally not subject to US withholding when services are performed outside the US).

-Vivek
